When an admin views the messages page this executes attacker-supplied JavaScript in the admin's session (stored XSS), enabling admin account compromise.

extra.message: The `message.message` field is rendered with `| safe` in the admin messages page. The message body is user-controlled via the authenticated feedback form (account_area/views.py send_feedback) and the unauthenticated API MessagesView.post (api/views.py:43-56). cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: `g.user.username` is rendered with `| safe` in the base navbar template. The username is user-controlled at account creation (User model / API UsersView.post) and never escaped, so a username containing HTML/JavaScript results in stored Cross-Site Scripting displayed on every authenticated page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The application explicitly disables the browser XSS auditor by setting `X-XSS-Protection: 0` by default (when `xss_protection_enabled` is not set in the session). This removes a browser-side defense-in-depth control against reflected XSS, amplifying the XSS vulnerabilities present in the app.

The Flask `SECRET_KEY` is hardcoded to a fixed, publicly-known value ('Keep it secret, keep it safe'). Since this key signs session cookies and Flask-Login remember tokens, an attacker who knows it can forge arbitrary session cookies and impersonate any user, including the admin.

Flask `DEBUG` mode is enabled in configuration. In debug mode the Werkzeug interactive debugger is exposed, which allows arbitrary Python code execution via the debugger console if the PIN is bypassed, and leaks source code and stack traces. This must never be enabled in production.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The `next` query parameter is taken directly from `request.args.get('next', ...)` and passed unvalidated to `redirect()`. An attacker can supply an absolute external URL (e.g. `?next=https://evil.com`) to redirect victims to an attacker-controlled site (Open Redirect), useful for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Passwords are stored and compared in plaintext (`user.password == password`). The User model stores the password as a plain string (app/models/models.py:11) and it is even exposed in the serialize() method and account page. No hashing (bcrypt/argon2) is used, so a database compromise exposes all credentials directly.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: User.serialize() includes the plaintext `password` field. This serialized data is returned by the API (UsersView.index and UsersView.get in app/blueprints/api/views.py), leaking user password hashes/plaintext to API consumers.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: MessagesView.post has no authentication/authorization decorator (unlike index/get/delete which use @admin_required). Any unauthenticated user can create Message records with attacker-controlled `message` and `from_user` fields. Because these fields are rendered with `| safe` in the admin messages page, this provides the injection vector for stored XSS against the admin (CWE-79) and constitutes a missing-authorization flaw.

is_owning_user compares `user.id == id` where `id` comes from the URL path as a string (FlaskView get/put in api/views.py:77,98) while `user.id` is an integer, so the ownership check generally fails or behaves inconsistently. More importantly, authorization for accessing/modifying user records relies solely on a client-supplied path `id` with no further validation, enabling Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control on the user API.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The add_admin management command defaults the admin password to the hardcoded value 'admin', creating an admin account with predictable credentials (admin/admin) if invoked without arguments.
